article_sentences: Counting of votes in 577 Zilla and 7,707 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies began at 8 a.m. on Saturday (November 7, 2026) amidst tight security.
Arrangements for the counting were made at 365 centres.

About 19,885 police officers of various capacities were deployed to ensure security keeping in view the likelihood of violence between cadres of the major political parties and the clashes jeopardising the counting process.
In East Godavari district, Damanthunigidem Panchayat of Devarapalli Mandal, 28-year-old Jana Sena Party MPTC contestant, Garapati Divya, died of cardiac arrest a few hours ahead of counting of votes.

stories.headline: Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
stories.title: Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives
stories.summary: The Supreme Court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7 and November 8, 2026 in Delhi-NCR

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on November 2, 2026 described bursting of firecrackers during Deepavali as a “religious practice” while permitting the use of green firecrackers for two days, on November 7 and November 8, in Delhi-NCR.

The unregulated use of firecrackers during Deepavali has historically led to a sharp rise in the Air Quality Index (AQI) and pollution levels, including the emission of particulate matter, the court observed.

“The right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond the Constitutional restrictions,” the Supreme Court held.
The state had “utterly failed” to comply with the Supreme Court’s orders issued since 2015 to impose restrictions on fireworks, the Bench said.
In fact, the situation had not improved even after the reimposition of a complete ban on firecrackers.
A significant spike in AQI levels was noticed on Dasara and the following day.
The “complete ban” had not only facilitated the illegal sale of firecrackers but had also prevented people from purchasing authorised green crackers, the court said.
The court had earlier suggested that the government enlist celebrities such as cricketer Virat Kohli to spread awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.

In October 2025, the apex court had permitted the sale and bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during Deepavali, subject to conditions aimed at balancing tradition with environmental and health concerns.
The court had then made it clear that the use of green crackers would be restricted to specified hours on the festival day and its eve.

The court permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 7, 2026 and the day after in the Delhi National Capital Region (Delhi-NCR).
“There shall not be any bursting of fireworks within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old age homes and any notified silence zones.

stories.headline: Ice breaks, tempers cool
stories.title: Ice breaks, tempers cool
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 6: Ice finally broke between disgruntled National Conference (NC) legislators and the party high command, including NC President Farooq Abdullah and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, after a meeting at the NC chief’s Gupkar residence in Srinagar on Friday, where the party high command assured the dissidents that it would address their grievances in phases. In his post-meeting interaction with reporters, Farooq Abdullah said: “We have spoken to them. Their problems were genuine, and we heard them properly. We will take some steps quickly and some steps slowly.” However, he rejected reports of a split, describing them as baseless, and said the NC had remained united and would not be broken. The three-time chief minister also reiterated the party’s commitment to the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood and Articles 370 and 35-A, saying the matter would be pursued in the Supreme Court. The meeting, in which around 15 to 16 legislators participated, was held against the backdrop of growing internal discontent within the party following the October 27 cabinet expansion. NC MLA Gurez, Nazir Ahmad Khan (Gurezi), said there was no breakaway group and that the legislators had received assurances from the party leadership. The legislators have authorisedGurezi to speak to the media on behalf of the group. Gurezi rejected suggestions that the legislators were attempting to establish a separate faction or political formation. “We are legislators of the National Conference. Whenever we have issues, we take them to our party leadership,” he said. Gurezi said that certain sections on social media had portrayed their earlier meetings as the emergence of a separate party, which was not the case. On the outcome of Friday’s meeting, he said: “There were certain issues which we brought before the Chief Minister (Omar Abdullah) Sahab and Farooq (Abdullah) Sahab. They have assured us that whether these are political issues or other matters, some will be addressed immediately while others will be resolved gradually.” The disgruntled NC legislators’ consultations began following the October 27 cabinet expansion. Their first closed-door meeting was held at the Humhama residence of MLA LolabQaysarJamshaid Lone, in which 17 NC legislators and an independent MLA from Thanamandi had reportedly pledged collective solidarity. The subsequent meetings were held at the TulsiBagh residence of MLA GurezNazir Ahmad Khan (Gurezi) and the Haiderpora residence of MLA GulmargPirzada Farooq Ahmad Shah. The November 5 meeting at HasnainMasoodi’sSanat Nagar residence was their fourth meeting since the cabinet expansion in which 20 legislators participated, 16 physically and four virtually. The disgruntled group had prepared a charter of demands covering governance, ministerial accountability, and organisational restructuring. Among the reported demands were greater efforts towards restoration of statehood and special status for Jammu and Kashmir; implementation of the Dachigam resolution concerning cabinet restructuring and ministerial accountability; changes in the Chief Minister’s inner circle; a consultative advisory group of two to three legislators to brief the Chief Minister regularly on governance and development; a high-powered disciplinary committee and an inquiry panel to address party grievances; strengthening the party’s media and communications machinery; regular meetings of the NC Working Committee; and establishment of an election cell and comprehensive organisational restructuring.
